title: Orthogonal reparametrization of the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson interest rate curve model: conditioning, diagnostics, and ide
summary: This paper proposes an orthogonal reparametrization technique for the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson (NSS) interest rate curve model to address ill-conditioning in the linear block when basis functions become nearly collinear. Using thin QR decomposition, the authors produce orthogonal linear parameters where the Fisher information matrix is diagonal, and derive a finite-horizon analytical orthogonalization with closed-form entries for the 4×4 continuous Gram matrix. Synthetic experiments and a U.S. Treasury study from 1981 to 2026 confirm the method yields smoother orthogonal parameter series.
key_points: The NSS model yields a separable nonlinear least-squares problem with an inner linear block that becomes ill-conditioned when basis functions are nearly collinear.
Thin QR decomposition produces orthogonal linear parameters where the Fisher information matrix is diagonal, conditional on nonlinear parameters.
A finite-horizon analytical orthogonalization on [0,T] yields closed-form entries for the 4×4 continuous Gram matrix involving exponentials, logarithms, and the exponential integral E1.
The QR element R44 serves as a scalar identifiability diagnostic and separates model reduction from numerical instability.
Orthogonalization preserves the least-squares fit and uncertainty of original linear parameters while isolating conditioning structure.
A daily U.S. Treasury study on a reduced fixed 9-tenor grid (1981–2026) demonstrates smoother orthogonal parameter series compared to classical NSS parameters.
why_it_matters: This methodological paper addresses numerical stability issues in fitting interest rate curves, which is foundational for yield curve construction and fixed income analytics. Practitioners and researchers using NSS models for curve fitting, risk management, or forecasting could benefit from this orthogonalization approach to avoid degenerate parameter estimates and improve model reliability. However, the paper is purely methodological and does not directly address market structure dynamics or macro catalysts.
